items.title: Finding the Equation of a Circle Given the Center and a Point on the Circle

sections.normalized_html: The circle above is centered at [MATH: C(2, 0)] and the point [MATH: X(-1, 4)] lies on the circumference. Find the equation of the circle.

sections.normalized_html:
The general equation of a circle with radius [MATH: r] centered at the point [MATH: (a,b)] is
[MATH: (x-a)^2 + (y-b)^2 = r^2.]

The length of the radius is

[MATH: CX|= sqrt((2 − (− 1))^{2} + (0 − 4)^{2}); = sqrt(3^{2} + 4^{2}); = sqrt(25); = 5.]

So, our circle is generated by the following equation: [MATH: (x − a)^{2} + (y − b)^{2}|= r^{2}; (x − 2)^{2} + (y − 0)^{2}|= 5^{2}; (x − 2)^{2} + y^{2}|= 25]
